verses.text: The boy Samuel served the LORD under Eli. In those days messages from the LORD were rare, and visions didn't happen often.
One night Eli had gone to lie down in his usual place. His eyesight had grown so dim he could barely see.
God's lamp was still burning, and Samuel had lain down in the LORD's temple, where God's ark was kept.
The LORD called Samuel, and Samuel answered, “Here I am.”
He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. You called me.” Eli said, “I didn't call you. Go lie down again.” So Samuel went back to bed.
The LORD called again, “Samuel!” Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am. You called me.” Eli answered, “I didn't call you, my son. Go lie down again.”
Samuel didn't yet know the LORD, because the LORD hadn't revealed his word to him yet.
The LORD called Samuel a third time. He got up and went to Eli. “Here I am. You called me.” Then Eli realized it was the LORD calling the boy.
Eli told Samuel, “Go lie down. If he calls you again, say, ‘Speak, LORD. Your servant is listening.’” So Samuel went back and lay down in his place.
The LORD came and stood there, calling out as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” Samuel answered, “Speak. Your servant is listening.”
The LORD told Samuel, “I'm about to do something in Israel that will make the ears of everyone who hears about it ring.
That day I'll carry out everything I said against Eli and his household, from beginning to end.
I told him I'd judge his family forever for the wrong he knew about. His sons brought a curse on themselves, and he did nothing to stop them.
That's why I swore to Eli's household that no sacrifice or offering would ever take away the guilt of his family.”
Samuel stayed in bed until morning, then opened the doors of the LORD's house. He was afraid to tell Eli about the vision.
Eli called him, “Samuel, my son!” He answered, “Here I am.”
Eli asked, “What did he say to you? Please don't hide it from me. May God deal with you severely if you hide anything he told you.”
So Samuel told him everything and held nothing back. Eli said, “He is the LORD. Let him do what seems good to him.”
Samuel grew up, and the LORD was with him. He let none of Samuel's words fall to the ground.
All Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel had been established as a prophet of the LORD.
The LORD continued to appear at Shiloh, where he revealed himself to Samuel through his word.
